transcript:
[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll keep this to 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya (PM): Priya here.
[00:10] Leo (Eng): Leo, yep.
[00:12] Maya (Infra): Maya, on the call.
[00:15] Samir (SE): Samir from Redwood.
[00:17] Daniel: Daniel, quick in and out.
[00:20] Avery: Awesome. Goal today is onboarding progress, access setup, and make sure we're green for the bench next week. I'll run through the checklist, Samir can call out any infra-specific items.
[00:30] Priya: Sounds good, we want to make sure the quality checks are realistic, but first infra.
[00:35] Samir: Quick update from our side: we validated the model artifact compatibility with your tokenization, small mismatch on whitespace handling but that's fixable in the client wrapper. More importantly, we need the service account and dev VPC access for the end-to-end KV cache tests.
[00:50] Leo: Right, so I tried to create the role last night but Maya and I weren't sure about the exact policies. Also question on whether the KMS key needs to be customer-managed with HSM vs. Redwood-managed.
[01:05] Maya: For production we'll need a CMK in our account; for the POC we can give you a test key but need to know if you call KMS directly or do envelope encryption.
[01:20] Samir: We support both. For the POC envelope encryption is easiest: Redwood will encrypt with a customer CMK via an API call; we do not require HSM unless you have strict compliance. If you prefer HSM we can support but that'll add some ops steps.
[01:40] Priya: Ok, can you send documentation on that? We need to show it to security.
[01:45] Avery: Absolutely, I'll send the security pack including SOC2 report, ISO attestations, and our pen test summary after the call.
[01:54] [small overlap] Maya: Great, also please include network architecture for the private deployment option.
[01:58] Avery: Will do.
[02:01] Samir: On the bench plan — for latency we want a couple of representative prompts, cold-cache and warm-cache runs, and then a sustained throughput run to map tokens/sec. We recommend 5k token long prompts as one of the upper-bound tests because your UI sometimes sends long contexts.
[02:20] Leo: Our current median prompt is 250 tokens but we have a tail up to 4k.
[02:25] Samir: Perfect, so we'll test 250 token and 4k token scenarios. Also need the sample prompt set and the dataset to run reranking and embeddings flow.
[02:38] Priya: I can share the top-5 prompt templates today and push the dataset to the S3 test bucket by Friday.
[02:45] Daniel: Quick note — some of the data has PII so we need to know retention policies.
[02:50] Avery: Our retention for POC buckets is short-lived, and we can set auto-delete. I'll include that in the security pack text.
[02:58] Maya: Also SSO — we need SAML metadata for the Redwood console for our security team. How long to set that up?
[03:06] Avery: It usually takes a day or two; we'll send the SP metadata and the config steps. Could you provide your IdP metadata?
[03:14] Maya: Yes, sending after this call.
[03:16] Leo: There was one test that failed in the earlier run — the KV cache wasn't being reused across batch boundaries, which spiked latency. Samir, any idea?
[03:25] Samir: Yeah, that sounded like the client was instantiating new sessions per request. We pushed a fix last week to keep the KV session pinned for 30s. We need you to update the client wrapper; I'll paste the snippet in the repo.
[03:38] Leo: Ok we'll take that.
[03:40] [crosstalk] Priya: And about cost — we are watching token spend, is there a way to estimate cost for warm-cache vs cold-cache?
[03:49] Avery: We have a cost model spreadsheet, I'll attach. Warm-cache will reduce compute tokens and so reduce cost per request materially. Samir: also batching and quantization profiles can help.
[04:03] Priya: Can we get recommendations for quantization? We are using a 7B open model currently.
[04:10] Samir: For 7B, 8-bit quantization is a good balance. We'll propose two profiles: perf-first and cost-first, and show expected latency and token cost.
[04:23] Leo: Any constraints around model variants? We might need fallback to a smaller model during peak load.
[04:29] Avery: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to a compatible smaller variant; we can configure that for the bench.
[04:36] Maya: One more security ask — can you provide audit log formats? We need to forward them into our SIEM.
[04:42] Samir: Yes, we emit structured audit logs with request id, model version, tokens, identity. I'll send sample logs.
[04:50] Priya: Good. For the bench scheduling, can we aim for Wed/Thu next week?
[04:55] Samir: I'll propose slots for Wed/Thu morning and afternoon.
[04:58] [00:05:00] Avery: Recap time — blockers: Leo/Maya to create service account + IAM and confirm KMS policy; Priya to upload prompts/dataset; Avery to send security pack and price spreadsheet; Samir to send benchmark plan and client fix snippet.
[05:20] Priya: That matches our notes.
[05:22] Leo: Quick question on SLOs: what latency SLO do you think is achievable for 250 token median?
[05:28] Samir: For a 7B quantized model on dedicated GPU we typically see median end-to-end 60-120ms token latency, end-to-end generation for 250 tokens should be in the 300-700ms ballpark depending on concurrency and batching. For hosted it might be slightly higher but we'll measure.
[05:45] Leo: Ok that helps set expectations.
[05:48] Maya: Anything else on compliance?
[05:50] Avery: No, just waiting on your KMS decision.
[05:53] Priya: Alright, thanks all. We'll aim to have access ready by Thursday.
[05:58] Avery: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the docs and action item list.
[06:02] [end of recording]
